newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.02 up at 42.15 to the dollar in the kerb market on Thursday because of a low demand for the U.S. currency before Friday's weekend, dealers said.
The rupee is likely to open lower on Saturday, one dealer at Khanani and Kalia International (pvt) Ltd said.
The State (central) bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 rupees to the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 5.00 percent after opening at 5.30 percent.
